item.text: {"text":"Evidence supports testing the objective before expanding history modeling, but does not establish the cause of weak Electronics separation. [Sampled-softmax analysis (2024)](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf) connects normalized representations and temperature to discriminative gradients and reduced influence from extremely hard, potentially false negatives; its reported temperature range of 0.1–0.2 is a starting point, not a benchmark guarantee. [gSASRec](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939) identifies sampled-BCE overconfidence and proposes generalized BCE. [eSASRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.06450) also supports sampled softmax within a strong SASRec-style system, although architecture changes prevent attributing its gains solely to loss. [MINE+/InfoNCE+](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.08520) provides a decoupled contrastive alternative, with less direct evidence for this sequential benchmark.\n\nPractical inference: retain the encoder initially; compare multi-negative BCE/gBCE, normalized sampled softmax, and a small decoupled-loss ablation under equal GPU budgets. Start with uniform negatives, then test a controlled random/semi-hard mixture; exclude known training positives and mask duplicate-target collisions. Hardness alone cannot distinguish difficult negatives from unobserved positives. [EMM (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0893608026004090) supports refreshed hard–random pools, while [ICLR 2025 research](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/2d2f85c0f93e69cf71f58eebaebb5e8d-Abstract-Conference.html) finds alignment can matter more than uniformity in sparse settings—so isotropy alone is insufficient. Diagnose embedding norms, mean cosine similarity, effective rank, and positive–negative margins using training data. Select exclusively by the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10; published gains do not establish transfer to its 99-negative evaluation."}
